entries.name: better-sqlite3
entries.use_for: Synchronous, fast SQLite bindings for Node.js
entries.why: Default SQLite driver for Node apps and ORMs

entries.name: Citus
entries.use_for: Distribute Postgres tables across nodes for scale-out
entries.why: Postgres extension for sharding and parallel distributed queries with full Postgres compatibility (multi-tenant SaaS, analytics).

entries.name: ClickHouse
entries.use_for: Column-oriented database for real-time analytics over billions of rows
entries.why: Leading open-source OLAP database (Apache-2.0)

entries.name: Diesel
entries.use_for: Compile-time checked ORM and query builder for Rust
entries.why: Mature, type-safe Rust ORM; complements SQLx already listed

entries.name: Drizzle ORM
entries.use_for: Type-safe SQL-like ORM for TypeScript on Postgres, MySQL and SQLite, including serverless drivers.
entries.why: Lightweight, SQL-first and edge-friendly; very popular in modern TS stacks with drizzle-kit migrations.

entries.name: DuckDB
entries.use_for: In-process analytical SQL database for querying Parquet, CSV and dataframes.
entries.why: The SQLite of analytics: fast columnar queries with bindings for Python, Node, R, WASM and more.

entries.name: etcd
entries.use_for: Strongly consistent distributed key-value store for config and coordination
entries.why: Raft-based KV store behind Kubernetes; watch API, leases and transactions for service discovery and leader election.

entries.name: FerretDB
entries.use_for: MongoDB-compatible API on top of PostgreSQL
entries.why: Open-source MongoDB alternative: speaks the Mongo wire protocol so existing drivers work, stores data in Postgres.

entries.name: goose
entries.use_for: Manage SQL and Go-function database migrations
entries.why: Simple migration tool supporting SQL files and Go functions, embeddable via io/fs, for Postgres, MySQL, SQLite and more.

entries.name: GORM
entries.use_for: Full-featured ORM for Go with associations, hooks and migrations
entries.why: The most popular Go ORM

entries.name: InfluxDB
entries.use_for: Store and query metrics, events and other time-series data
entries.why: Purpose-built time-series database (v3 core in Rust on Arrow/Parquet) with SQL querying.

entries.name: Knex.js
entries.use_for: SQL query builder with migrations and seeds for Postgres, MySQL, SQLite and more
entries.why: Most-downloaded SQL query builder for Node; base layer for Objection.js and others

entries.name: Kysely
entries.use_for: Type-safe SQL query builder for TypeScript.
entries.why: Full SQL control with inferred types and no codegen; a common choice when you want a query builder, not an ORM.

entries.name: migrate
entries.use_for: Run versioned database migrations from a CLI or Go code
entries.why: Widely used migration tool with drivers for Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, Mongo, ClickHouse and more; sources from files, S3, GitHub.

entries.name: MikroORM
entries.use_for: TypeScript ORM using Data Mapper, Unit of Work and Identity Map patterns.
entries.why: Strong choice for domain-heavy apps needing transactional unit-of-work semantics.

entries.name: Mongoose
entries.use_for: Model MongoDB data with schemas, validation and middleware in Node.js
entries.why: The default MongoDB ODM for Node.js, with millions of weekly downloads

entries.name: Neon
entries.use_for: Self-host serverless Postgres with branching and scale-to-zero
entries.why: Separates Postgres storage and compute for instant database branching and autoscaling; the open core behind Neon.

entries.name: node-postgres
entries.use_for: PostgreSQL client for Node.js.
entries.why: The standard Postgres driver for Node; underlies many ORMs and query builders.

entries.name: PGlite
entries.use_for: Run real Postgres embedded in the browser, Node or Bun via WASM.
entries.why: Full Postgres in a few MB with no server; great for tests, local-first apps and prototypes.

entries.name: Postgres.js
entries.use_for: Fast PostgreSQL client for Node, Deno and Bun using tagged-template SQL
entries.why: Fast, full-featured Postgres client for JS; a common Drizzle driver

entries.name: PostgreSQL
entries.use_for: The default open-source relational database for new apps
entries.why: Official mirror of PostgreSQL: mature, extensible RDBMS with JSONB, full-text search and a huge extension ecosystem.

license_verified.note: COPYRIGHT file contains the PostgreSQL License (OSI-approved)

entries.name: Prisma ORM
entries.use_for: Schema-first ORM for Node.js and TypeScript with generated type-safe client and migrations.
entries.why: Mature and widely adopted, with strong DX: declarative schema, Prisma Migrate and Studio.

entries.name: Redis
entries.use_for: In-memory data store for caching, queues, pub/sub and vector search
entries.why: The reference in-memory data structure server; Redis 8+ is available under AGPLv3 (tri-licensed with RSALv2/SSPL).

license_verified.note: Redis 8+ tri-licensed RSALv2/SSPLv1/AGPLv3; the AGPLv3 option is OSI-approved

entries.name: RocksDB
entries.use_for: Embed a fast persistent key-value store in your application
entries.why: Meta's LSM-tree storage engine used inside TiKV, Kafka Streams and many databases; dual GPLv2/Apache-2.0.

entries.name: Sequelize
entries.use_for: Promise-based ORM for Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite and SQL Server
entries.why: Long-standing, very widely installed Node.js ORM

entries.name: SQLAlchemy
entries.use_for: The Python SQL toolkit and ORM.
entries.why: The standard Python ORM; used under FastAPI and Flask apps, with Alembic for migrations.

entries.name: SQLx
entries.use_for: Async Rust SQL toolkit with compile-time checked queries for Postgres, MySQL and SQLite.
entries.why: Most popular Rust database crate; checks raw SQL against your schema at build time.

entries.name: Supabase
entries.use_for: Hosted or self-hosted Postgres platform with auth, storage, realtime and auto-generated APIs.
entries.why: Fastest path to a production Postgres backend; open source and self-hostable, with SDKs for many languages.

entries.name: TDengine
entries.use_for: High-throughput time-series database for IoT and industrial data
entries.why: Time-series DB with built-in caching, stream processing and SQL; designed for billions of IIoT data points.

entries.name: TiDB
entries.use_for: MySQL-compatible distributed SQL database that scales horizontally
entries.why: Distributed ACID SQL with HTAP (TiFlash) and vector search; MySQL protocol so existing drivers and ORMs keep working.

entries.name: Turso
entries.use_for: SQLite-compatible embedded database rewritten in Rust
entries.why: Ground-up SQLite rewrite with async I/O, concurrent writes and vector search, keeping file and SQL compatibility.

entries.name: TypeORM
entries.use_for: Decorator-based ORM for Node.js supporting many SQL databases and MongoDB.
entries.why: Long-standing ORM, default in many NestJS projects, supports Active Record and Data Mapper.

entries.name: Valkey
entries.use_for: High-performance key-value store for caching, queues and realtime data, compatible with Redis clients.
entries.why: BSD-licensed Linux Foundation fork of Redis, backed by major cloud vendors.
